note: Original description by Wasmann 1911 (Revue Zoologique Africaine, as Cubitermes sulcifrons); the measurements and comparative text for the soldier and worker are taken from Emerson's 1928 redescription. The text was extracted by OCR from the Internet Archive scan; the Wasmann original is in German.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: (Placed in the genus Cubitermes in the original.) Wing span 30—32 mm; body length with wings 19—20 mm; wing length 15 mm, width nearly 5 mm; body length without wings 9.5—10 mm, width 2.5 mm. Upper surface pale brown, weakly shining except on the head, the yellow pilosity denser and longer than in C. fungifaber and C. zenkeri. Head with the projecting compound eyes almost as wide as the pronotum, length to the labrum slightly less than the width; compound eyes smaller than in fungifaber; ocelli large, transversely oval, separated from the compound eye by more than their diameter. Frons flatly concave, with a large circular fontanelle pit with a raised rim, and a strong longitudinal ridge in front of the pit. Postclypeus (epistomum) strongly convex, three times as wide as long, anterior margin strongly sinuate, much shorter and more convex than in fungifaber. Labrum large, slightly wider than long, rounded in front. Antenna 16 segments, stout, extending beyond the posterior margin of the pronotum; segments 3 and 4 smaller and narrower than the adjacent ones, segments 5—11 gradually longer, segments 5 and 6 square, the following segments about 1.5 times as long as wide and nearly equal in length. Pronotum nearly semicircular, twice as wide as long, the sides gradually rounded, the posterior margin much wider than in fungifaber; the transverse groove near the anterior margin ends at the depressed, forward-sloping anterior corners, the median longitudinal groove very shallow, the posterior margin neither concave nor notched. Wings pale brown, relatively short and very broad, only 3 times as long as wide; forewing 15 mm long and 4.8 mm wide, hindwing 14.5 mm long and 5 mm wide; brown veins distinct, the subcosta accompanied by a dark line that disappears at the middle of the wing; at the apical quarter of the forewing the subcosta gives off a row of fine sinuate cross-veins, whereas in the hindwing at the apical third it gives off a short, stout, strongly curved branch that runs into the outer margin of the wing near the apex of the subcosta; media forks at the middle of the wing and curves slightly downwards apically, with 3 simple branches in the forewing, and in the hindwing splits into 2 branches at the middle, each of which then divides into 2; submedia (cubitus) strongly curved downwards, with 8 simple branches.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Sides of the head straight, slightly convergent anteriorly, posterior margin only weakly rounded. Antenna 15 segments, segment 3 shorter than segment 4, segment 4 slightly shorter than segment 2. Labrum very deeply incised, the two lobes very thin. Mandibles rather strongly curved. Anterior margin of the pronotum slightly concave. Measurements: head length including the mandibles 5.80 mm; head length to the apex of the labrum 4.40 mm; head length to behind the antennal bases 2.80 mm; head width 2.54 mm; antennal length 5.20 mm; pronotum length 0.64 mm, width 1.30 mm; hind tibia length 2.18 mm; left mandible length 2.80 mm; curvature of the left mandible (distance from the line joining the mandibular apex and the basal process to the point of greatest curvature) 0.40 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Antenna 15 segments. Head width 1.32 mm; hind tibia length 1.50 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Locality: Cameroon (Senegambina, collected by R. N. Evans, 1920-4-24). Emerson redescribed the species from 1 soldier and several workerless soldiers (ergatoid workers), noting that the cotypes have a shallower labral incision and are otherwise identical; it is very close to M. intercalatus, but the latter has a shallower labral incision, more curved and slightly shorter mandibles; it is similar to the description of M. kemneri, but the latter has only slightly curved mandibles and the anterior lobe of the pronotum is not incised in the middle; it is very close to M. hamatus but larger. The queen has body length 30 mm and width 10 mm, pale yellow, the forebody and tergites brown, the tergites almost 3 mm wide, the pilosity largely worn away so that the forebody is shinier.
